annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "tap" on page 202 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
Gordon, John. Finnegans Blog (Tavern chapters). https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Mamalujo signal "Leinster" on page 202 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the Four Old Men — Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; Ulster, Munster, Leinster, Connaught — serve here as senile chroniclers and bedpost witnesses during the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. In this Age of Gods (closing) passage, they observe and record the dream's events as squawking gulls circling overhead.
sources: O'Donovan, John. The Annals of the Four Masters. https://celt.ucc.ie/published/T100005A/
MacCabe, Colin. James Joyce and the Revolution of the Word. https://archive.org/details/jamesjoycerevolu0000macc
FWEET: Mamalujo / Four Old Men concordance. https://www.fweet.org
Ricorso.net: James Joyce Critical Archive. https://www.ricorso.net
